title: A Simple Effective Method for Deadlock Prevention of S3PR, GS3PR, and S4PR Petri Net Models of Automated Manufacturing Systems
content: There exists a huge quantity of papers written about deadlock prevention of Automated Manufacturing Systems (AMS) by means Petri net (PN)-based models in the world literature. In principle they consist in two approaches, namely based either on P-invariants or on siphons of Petri net (PN) models of AMS. The approach presented here makes use of the former approach simultaneously with the structure of deadlocks themselves acquired by means of the reachability tree (RT) of such models. This approach unifies structure of all deadlocks of the AMS PN model as to activity (i.e. operation) places in order to construct the basic matrix [L] used in P-invariant approach making the supervisor synthesis possible. Namely, the product of the matrix [L] with the incidence matrix [N] of the PN model directly yields the incidence matrix [N]s of the supervisor which guarantees deadlock-freeness of the supervised system. In such a way the application of the only one supervisor is able to prevent all deadlocks in the actual model. The approach is verified by means of its application on quite a number of Petri net models of AMS of type S3PR, GS3PR and S4PR. In several cases, the results obtained by the proposed approach are compared with those obtained by the siphon-based approach. The comparison is based on the confrontation of the RTs of supervised models obtained by both approaches. Finally, the possibility of decomposition (or rather splitting) of the supervisor in the case of the structure of very complex S4PR PN models into two supervisors is shown, if in the case of using a single supervisor, the development of one of the two parts of the model (production lines) is suppressed at the expense of the other (as far as access to resources is concerned).
